authorityNote: This file is machine-readable governance CONFIG. It is NOT a governance authority and it outranks nothing. Authority order remains: GOVERNANCE_REWRITE_2026_06_10/LETBUYY_CONSTITUTION.md (supreme) > AGENTS.md > nested AGENTS.md > LETBUYY_CANONICAL_SYSTEMS.md. Where this file and any of those disagree, those win and the disagreement is a defect in this file.
purpose: Declare the expected Android applicationId and namespace for every native-Android Flutter app, in a file that is NOT generated from and does NOT live beside the Gradle files it governs. Changing a shipped identity now requires a reviewable diff to TWO files, not a silent edit to one. This exists because apps/admin_app/android/app/build.gradle.kts carried applicationId "com.letbuyy.letbuyy" — the customer app's shipped identity — undetected through Phase 0 and fourteen further phases, found only by a human diffing two files by hand. See docs/migration/repository_consolidation/27_android_gradle_resolution.md.
honestyContract: com.letbuyy.letbuyy (customer_app) is a SHIPPED Play Store production identity. Its signingConfig references a real release keystore (apps/customer_app/android/key.properties, untracked, storeFile=key.jks). This is the one value in this file that cannot be changed and re-issued if it is ever lost or altered.

com.letbuyy.admin (admin_app) is a RETIRED identity, recorded under retiredApps below rather than apps. It was never a shipped identity: its release signingConfig pointed at debug.keystore. apps/admin_app's Flutter/Firestore implementation, including its whole android/ tree, was deleted in phase FB-1 (2026-09-05) under the owner's decision to retire Firebase completely, so there is no longer a Gradle file to check. The identity is kept on record so it can never be silently reused: the validator now fails if ANY tracked Gradle script in the repository declares a retired applicationId.

com.letbuyy.store (merchant_app) is declared in Kotlin DSL (build.gradle.kts), not Groovy — this is the only one of the three apps that is. A check that assumes Groovy syntax will silently pass merchant_app while verifying nothing.

namespace and applicationId are independent Gradle/AGP concerns and may legitimately differ. This was recorded for admin_app, whose namespace was com.letbuyy.letbuyy while its applicationId was com.letbuyy.admin — documented scaffolding leftover, not a defect. That app's Gradle tree was deleted in FB-1; the principle is kept because it still governs the remaining apps and the next reader would otherwise 'fix' a legitimate divergence.

This registry does not declare versionCode or versionName. Those change on every release by design; asserting an exact value here would need editing on every release cycle and would be a worse validator than none.

This registry does not declare signingConfig key material or any keystore/key.properties content. The validator enforces only that no such file is TRACKED IN GIT (a path-level check) — it never reads, prints, diffs or hashes their contents. See the disclosed incident in docs/migration/repository_consolidation/27_android_gradle_resolution.md where a diff against a non-existent tracked counterpart printed a real keystore password.

customer_app.shippedNote: Play Store production identity. Real release signingConfig (not debug).

merchant_app.shippedNote: Uses a different, environment-variable-driven signing setup (releaseKeystorePath in build.gradle.kts, no key.properties file at all — unlike customer_app/admin_app). Shipped status was NOT determined this phase; recorded honestly as unknown rather than guessed. Out of Phase S's scope beyond recording the currently-declared applicationId/namespace.

admin_app.retiredReason: apps/admin_app was 100% Firestore-backed with no canonical gateway client, and had never shipped a signed release (its release signingConfig pointed at debug.keystore). Its source, including the entire android/ tree and google-services.json, was deleted and the root reduced to the RESERVED manifest-only shape. See apps/admin_app/AGENTS.md.
admin_app.enforcement: No tracked build.gradle or build.gradle.kts anywhere in this repository may declare this applicationId. Reusing a retired identity for a different app would silently ship one product under another's Play Store listing.
